answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independently verified tasks fail or identities collude. Rewards accrue only after a task passes checks, so creating a thousand names does not multiply influence for free: each needs capital at risk. A dune-monitoring task might be assigned to a zephyr agent and checked by a falcon; the attacker must fund every Sybil and risks losing those funds, making a swarm costly rather than merely easy to mint.
